classification_policy.build-time-only: The exact tag is consumed by an importer, builder, registration gate, or generated-resource policy rather than a live rule.
classification_policy.deferred: The tag is valid source evidence, but its first gameplay consumer belongs to a named later phase.
classification_policy.not-applicable: The source tag describes an integration or behavior that CrucibleCraft intentionally does not implement.
classification_policy.rule-input: The exact tag is suitable for a MaterialRule predicate or another runtime behavior decision.

removed.COOLING: No direct source-backed packet consumer exists; a later cooling system must introduce its own proven contract.

removed.ROTATION: GT6 RU is intentionally represented by the existing KINETIC packet type.

extruder_compaction_decision.decision: Keep the replay-verified sparse relation until MaterialRule can express all source gates. A compact migration needs at least 27 IO variants plus sparse duration overrides; splitting EXTRUDABLE_SIMPLE EU/t yields about 54 rules. Replacing it with one PROCESSING.EXTRUDABLE rule per shape would add and remove recipes.

completed_safety_backfill.effect: A missing registered form on a processing target is now an explicit non-match; an unguarded required target resource remains a load error.

legacy_rule_condition_backfill.decision: Existing broad rules remain source-compatible until their owning phase can prove the exact predicate and expansion delta. A raw tag-name match is not sufficient evidence.
